$comment: EVERY SCRIPT THAT ASKS GIT WHICH FILES EXIST OR CHANGED DECLARES WHAT IT DOES ABOUT
UNTRACKED ONES (#899). git ls-files, git diff and git status --porcelain all answer a
question about the repository, and a branch that ADDS a file is invisible to the first
two until it is committed. That is precisely the moment someone runs the checker: you
have just written the file, you ask about your change, and the answer is about a tree
that does not contain your work.
THE HOLE WAS FOUND AND PATCHED THREE SEPARATE TIMES — census (#209), classify (#224),
assert-formatted (#856) — and census's own comment records that the lesson did not even
travel between two files the same author wrote back to back. Ten more patches would
leave the eleventh script, written next month, with the same hole and nothing to catch
it. So the deliverable is a declared stance, not a uniform behaviour.
IT CANNOT FAIL IN CI, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDS A GATE. Measured: an installed-and-built
worktree has ZERO untracked non-ignored files, so in a clean checkout the gap never
appears. This class only ever costs a human, and only at the moment they most need the
answer.
STANCES:
examined      the script looks at untracked files and accounts for them. NOT taken on
trust: the gate requires the source to actually pass `--others`, so this
is a corroborated claim rather than a promise.
out-of-scope  the script deliberately does not look, because its subject genuinely is
the committed tree. `why` must say what that subject is.
unexamined    a known gap, not a decision. Requires an open issue in `lifts`, the same
convention checks.json uses, so it cannot quietly become permanent.
`why` IS MANDATORY AND THAT IS THE POINT. The model is NOT_PUBLIC in
public-api-completeness.test.ts: an exemption you cannot add without writing its reason
stays a decision instead of becoming a reflex.

scripts/assert-armed-prs-are-covered-by-.why: IT ASKS GIT NOTHING. Its only child process is `spawnSync("gh", ...)`; the string "git" appears nowhere in the file. The classifier matches SOURCE TEXT — `src.includes('"status"')` — and the single occurrence is a CAPTURED GitHub payload quoted in a comment at :882, `{ "conclusion": "", "status": "QUEUED" }`, which #1139 quotes verbatim because a paraphrased fixture only tests its author's belief about the wire. So the over-inclusion this classifier declares as deliberate did exactly what its header says it will, and the honest record is that the match is a quotation rather than an invocation. NOTED, BECAUSE IT IS THE FIRST DECLARED ENTRY THAT EXISTS ONLY BECAUSE OF A COMMENT: if that becomes common the list stops meaning `scripts that ask git which files exist` and starts meaning `files that quote the word`, at which point the population is the thing to fix rather than the roster.

scripts/assert-fork-python-imports-resol.why: same severability subject: imports must resolve in the tree a fork receives, and `ls-files` IS that tree. Widening it would make an untracked module satisfy an import that a fork would not have, which inverts the property rather than strengthening it.

scripts/assert-formatted.mjs.why: its subject is THE CHANGE, so a branch that adds files is exactly what it must cover. It reports the breakdown and REFUSES (exit 2) when an untracked file in its subject is unformatted — the case where committing would turn its PASS into a FAIL (#856).

scripts/assert-git-subject-stances.mjs.why: IT IS IN ITS OWN SUBJECT, by construction rather than by exemption: its detection matches the literal "ls-files", which appears in it. Written with `git ls-files` alone it reported PASS over 13 scripts and could not see the fourteenth — itself, uncommitted. A NEW git-subject script is exactly what must not slip through, and a new script is untracked when its author runs this.

scripts/assert-no-install-blocking-paths.why: the property is what a FRESH CHECKOUT contains, and a fresh checkout contains the tracked set exactly. An uncommitted file cannot break someone else's clone until it is committed.

scripts/assert-no-missing-workspace-invo.why: it is a fork-severability property stated over the tree a fork would receive, which is the tracked set. An untracked workflow file is not yet part of what anyone forks.

scripts/assert-no-nul-in-text-sources.mj.why: its subject is the COMMITTED tree, and that is the scope the defect actually has. A raw NUL matters because it makes a file binary to whoever searches it LATER — a reviewer on another branch, an agent grepping for a token. An uncommitted file has no such reader yet, and the author already has the bytes in front of them. Scanning untracked files would also drag in every build artefact, coverage dump and downloaded fixture in a working tree, which are binary by design and would bury the one finding this exists to surface.

scripts/assert-no-silent-skips.mjs.why: A GAP, NOT A DECISION. Its subject is 'a test that never runs anywhere must say why', and the moment that question gets asked is when someone has just WRITTEN a test — which is untracked. It answers about a tree without it and says PASS.

scripts/assert-no-undeclared-reverts.mjs.why: its subject is the diff BETWEEN TWO COMMITS. An untracked file is in neither, so there is no sense in which it could be part of the comparison — this is not a gap, it is the subject being commits rather than a working tree.

scripts/assert-overrides-entail-declarat.why: ITS SUBJECT IS EVERY WORKSPACE MANIFEST, and a branch that ADDS a workspace adds a package.json that is untracked until someone commits. A new workspace declaring a range an override violates is exactly the case this check exists for, so a version that cannot see new files is the version that passes precisely when it matters. It therefore passes `--others --exclude-standard --cached` to `git ls-files` and reads tracked and untracked manifests alike. It does not refuse on an untracked file — an unparseable manifest refuses wherever it came from, and a parseable new one is simply in the subject.

scripts/assert-rung5-security-patches.mj.why: its subject is a VENDORED, PINNED subtree whose contents are asserted against upstream. An untracked file there is local scratch, not part of the vendored artifact under assertion.

scripts/assert-sibling-tests-are-owned.m.why: A GAP, NOT A DECISION. Adding a test beside a rung-owned source file is exactly the act this checks, and a newly added test is untracked at the moment its author would run this.

scripts/census.mjs.why: its whole job is to notice NEW arrivals under frozen globs, so a brand-new file is the case it exists for. Exits 2 INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS when it finds one (#209).

scripts/classify.mjs.why: it must not report PASS over untracked rung-owned files, for the same reason as the census: a file's rung is a question people ask about a file they just wrote (#224).

scripts/eject-audit-run.mjs.why: it drives eject.mjs and inherits its subject, and uses `git status --porcelain` for the same dirty-tree refusal rather than to enumerate a subject.

scripts/eject.mjs.why: it ejects the committed tree and leaves a repo someone could have cloned. Untracked files are not in a clone. It already REFUSES on a dirty tree via `git status --porcelain`, which is the stronger guard: rather than silently ignoring local work, it declines to run over it.

scripts/run-checks.mjs.why: it passes `--untracked-files=no` explicitly. The status call establishes whether the tree is dirty for provenance in the run header; it does not enumerate a subject, and untracked scratch is deliberately not treated as making a run dirty.
